svg.title: Draw the receipt
svg.desc: A large empty frame split by a dashed horizontal line, labelled forward with an arrow above the line and backward with a reversed arrow below it. A panel underneath lists what a good answer looks like: one block per value with its shape written on, forward arrows in one colour above the line, backward arrows dashed and reversed below it, the grad_fn name on each arrow such as MmBackward0, one real number on the backward path such as minus 0.09975049, .item() drawn as a door out with the receipt left behind, and a note that .grad adds so 6 plus 27 equals 33.
svg.text: One tensor, the operations done to it, and the slope coming back.
What a good answer looks like
· one block per value, each with its shape written on
· forward arrows in one colour, above the dashed line
· backward arrows dashed and reversed, below it
· the grad_fn name on each arrow: MmBackward0, and so on
· one real number on the backward path, e.g. −0.09975049
· .item() drawn as a door out, with the receipt left behind
